memory_candidates.content: verify-deploy.sh Gate 20 (orchestrator context budget lock) compares a live-predicted eager-load byte total (measure-eager-context.sh, source-store-only prediction of the regenerated CLAUDE.md + eager rules) against a fixed, dated, manually-reviewed eager_load.baseline_bytes in orchestrator-context-budget.json. Any new eager-loaded content (e.g. a one-line Command Reference row added to merge-sources/claudemd.md) can push the live total over the recorded baseline even though the addition itself is tiny -- the fix is NOT re-deriving the baseline from the new measurement casually, but a reviewed, dated note entry following that file's own established per-addition convention (first try to trim redistributable duplication elsewhere in the new content; only if none exists, round the new total up to the next 100 B and record why).

A test suite asserting a binary's ABSENCE from PATH (e.g. 'piper is not installed, confirm fallback behavior') must build a fully self-contained isolated bin directory (every real coreutils dependency symlinked in once from the test process's own PATH, PLUS the bare interpreter used to invoke the subject script resolved once via `command -v bash` before PATH is narrowed) and set PATH to ONLY that directory with no real-PATH fallback. A 'fakebin:$PATH' style PATH silently lets a genuinely-installed system binary (piper/paplay/espeak-ng are commonly present on a NixOS dev host) leak through and defeat the absence assertion -- the test can pass for the wrong reason, or fail outright if the real binary behaves differently than the fake.

A bash helper using `find "$dir" -maxdepth 1 -name PATTERN ... | sort | head | cut` to find the newest matching file degrades safely under `set -e`/`pipefail` when $dir EXISTS but has zero matches (find exits 0, empty output) -- but NOT when $dir was never created at all: find then exits non-zero before the pipe even starts, and pipefail propagates that failure, aborting the whole script. Guard with `[ -d "$dir" ] || return 0` before the find call whenever the directory's existence is not already guaranteed by an earlier step in the same run.

sapience_notes.subject: orchestrate-recap.sh deploy-root-guard self-correct
sapience_notes.value: deploy-root-guard.sh's DEPLOY_ROOT_GUARD_SELF_CORRECT=1 opt-in widens REPO_ROOT via a validated git-toplevel candidate, but a script that derives its own working root via lib/common.sh's common_repo_root() (a pure N-levels-up computation) ignores that widened REPO_ROOT entirely and recomputes a naive, wrong path when invoked bare from the agent-system source store. Only a small number of scripts (sync-manifest-scripts.sh, check-extension-docs.sh) are written to consume $REPO_ROOT directly after sourcing the guard; an ordinary deployed-only script (the orchestrate-*.sh family) is not self-correcting and must be smoke-tested via a fake .claude/scripts/ tree or CORE_TEST_SUBJECT_MODE=source-store, never via the self-correct env var alone.

sapience_notes.subject: measure-eager-context.sh vs verify-deploy.sh gate 20 baseline check
sapience_notes.value: measure-eager-context.sh --check only validates there are no volatile-file hits; it does NOT itself compare the live total against orchestrator-context-budget.json's eager_load.baseline_bytes. That comparison lives inside verify-deploy.sh's own gate20_run function, which reads BUDGET_CONFIG from $TARGET/agent-system/extensions/core/context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json directly (the SOURCE STORE path, not a deployed copy), so editing that JSON takes effect immediately without a redeploy.

sapience_notes.subject: check-extension-docs.sh README-command-mention rule
sapience_notes.value: check-extension-docs.sh's check_readme_vs_manifest() fails loudly if any command name in manifest.json's provides.commands array is not textually mentioned (as /<name>) in that extension's own README.md -- this check runs independently of, and is not anticipated by, a plan's own Files-to-modify list when a plan adds a new command but only updates merge-sources/claudemd.md (the CLAUDE.md merge source) without also touching the extension's top-level README.md.

sapience_notes.subject: dead-command-recommendation lint shape
sapience_notes.value: lint-dead-command-recommendations.sh's Layer 2 shape requires a recommendation line to read 'Next:' (optionally followed by 'Run') or the standalone word 'Run' directly followed by '/<name>', after stripping markdown emphasis characters. A results-template Next Steps line recommending a new command must use exactly this shape (e.g. 'Run /recap') to be recognized as a real, checkable recommendation rather than silently exempt as non-matching prose.

sapience_notes.subject: git-commit-phase.sh Containment Self-Check and __WHOLE_TREE__
sapience_notes.value: A task's declared file_scope containing the literal sentinel __WHOLE_TREE__ (used by a plan phase that invokes whole-tree regeneration, e.g. a deploy-headless.sh phase) is NOT treated as a wildcard match by git-commit-phase.sh's Containment Self-Check -- a genuinely out-of-scope path (not individually listed in file_scope) is still dropped and warned on even when __WHOLE_TREE__ is present in that same file_scope array. The sentinel is a declarative marker for human/plan readers, not a predicate the mechanical containment check interprets specially.
